requirements.statement: Persistence is real and lifecycle-tested against a real Postgres, not a mock
The ownership boundary is enforced: a member cannot read or mutate another member's task
The accessibility budget is kept even though the profile makes it optional for an internal tool
requirements.source: internal-crud profile, accessibility (deliberately kept required in this app's readiness manifest)

requirements.statement: The audit trail records who changed which task, when, and what changed
The primary flow works end to end: sign in, manage own tasks, sign out
requirements.source: PP-004 acceptance (a second, materially different golden stack reaches R3)

requirements.statement: The app is deployable as a pinned, reproducible container image built from zero
Database migrations are forward-and-back safe through a real Alembic downgrade, and the rollback is rehearsed
No secrets are committed to the repository
Both production dependency trees, Python and JavaScript, carry no unaddressed findings
Both builds are reproducible from lockfiles and an SBOM describes each side of what shipped
The app is observable in production: structured logs and a health endpoint that is actually exercised
requirements.source: R3 control set, observability and health-check

requirements.statement: Deploy, diagnose, incident and recovery steps are written down for an operator who did not build this
The threat boundary and the controls that defend it are documented
Authentication endpoints resist credential-stuffing and brute-force attempts

exception.reason: There is no rate limiting on /api/auth/login inside the app. A network or edge rate limiter is expected to sit in front of it in production, and this reference app does not ship the deployment layer that would provide one, so the control is out of its own boundary rather than forgotten.
exception.compensatingControl: Password hashing costs per attempt (backend/app/auth.py); docs/runbook.md names the edge rate limiter as a deployment prerequisite.

requirements.statement: Mutating requests cannot be forged from another origin

exception.reason: There is no CSRF token. The app relies on samesite lax on the session cookie plus a required application/json content type on every mutating request, which together block the simple cross-site form attack but are weaker than a token if the app ever grows a form-based mutation path.
exception.compensatingControl: samesite=lax on the session cookie (backend/app/auth.py) and a JSON-only mutation surface.

requirements.statement: The session signing secret can be rotated without logging every user out

exception.reason: There is a single SESSION_SECRET and no grace-period rollover with two valid keys, so rotating it invalidates every session at once. Accepted at this app's size: the operational cost is a forced re-login, which docs/runbook.md documents as the expected consequence.
exception.compensatingControl: docs/runbook.md states the blast radius of a rotation, so an operator is not surprised by it.

requirements.statement: An unauthenticated browser is denied the authenticated area before any of it is served
requirements.source: docs/security-notes.md, Known limitations (the route-guard difference from PP-003)

exception.reason: FastAPI cannot distinguish routes inside a static SPA bundle, so /tasks always serves index.html and the React app redirects client-side after /api/tasks returns 401. An unauthenticated browser therefore briefly receives the app shell HTML and JS, which PP-003's Next.js middleware denies at the edge. Accepted for this reference app because the difference is what is shipped before the redirect, not what is reachable.
exception.compensatingControl: The real authorization boundary is the API layer and is identical to PP-003's: backend/app/guard.py, proven by the ownership-boundary tests in backend/tests/integration/test_api.py. No data is served with the shell.

requirements.statement: Traffic to the application is encrypted in transit and the browser is told to keep it that way
requirements.source: OWASP ASVS 5.0.0 L1 V3.4.1, V12.1.1, V12.2.1, V12.2.2 via docs/evidence/security-baseline.json

exception.reason: The application speaks plain HTTP inside its container and emits no Strict-Transport-Security header. TLS termination, certificate issuance and protocol-version policy belong to an edge this reference app deliberately does not ship, which is the same boundary the rate-limiting exception draws. Accepted as an app-boundary decision rather than an oversight; a deployment that skips the edge is running it wrong.
exception.compensatingControl: docs/runbook.md names the reverse proxy as a deployment prerequisite, and the session cookie is issued with the Secure attribute whenever the app runs in production mode.

requirements.statement: Browser-side defences are configured: response context controls and clearing authenticated data at session end
requirements.source: OWASP ASVS 5.0.0 L1 V3.2.1, V14.3.1 via docs/evidence/security-baseline.json

exception.reason: No Content-Security-Policy, X-Content-Type-Options, Referrer-Policy or frame-ancestors directive is emitted, and nothing clears the SPA's in-memory React state or sends Clear-Site-Data when the session ends. Surfaced by the ASVS baseline on 2026-09-23; it was never recorded before because the prose security notes only listed what the app does, never what it omits.
exception.compensatingControl: Every API response is JSON with a JSON content type, the app renders no untrusted HTML and uses no framing, and the session cookie is httpOnly so client-side script cannot read it.

requirements.statement: The session cookie name itself signals the security properties the browser must enforce
requirements.source: OWASP ASVS 5.0.0 L1 V3.3.1 via docs/evidence/security-baseline.json

exception.reason: The cookie is named "session" with neither the __Host- nor the __Secure- prefix. Adopting __Host- requires Secure on every response, which would stop the app working over plain HTTP in local development and in the container rehearsal, so the change is a development-workflow decision rather than a one-line fix.
exception.compensatingControl: The cookie is already httpOnly, sameSite=lax, path-scoped to / and marked Secure in production, which is what the prefix would have forced.

requirements.statement: Signing out actually ends the session, and a captured session token stops working
requirements.source: OWASP ASVS 5.0.0 L1 V7.2.4, V7.4.1 via docs/evidence/security-baseline.json

exception.reason: The session is a self-contained signed token and logout only deletes the cookie, so a token captured beforehand keeps being accepted for the rest of its 8-hour lifetime, and re-authenticating does not invalidate the previous one. Fixing it means a terminated-token list, a per-user signing key or a switch to reference tokens — an architecture change, not a patch. Surfaced by the ASVS baseline on 2026-09-23 and the most serious thing it found.
exception.compensatingControl: The token lifetime is capped at 8 hours, it is httpOnly and sameSite=lax so script cannot read it and it is not sent on cross-site navigations, and it is Secure in production so it does not travel in clear text.

requirements.statement: A user can change their own password
requirements.source: OWASP ASVS 5.0.0 L1 V6.2.2 via docs/evidence/security-baseline.json

exception.reason: The application has no change-password function at all: accounts exist because the seed created them. This is a missing feature of a reference app built to exercise the pack contract, not a defect in an implemented flow, but a user genuinely cannot rotate a credential they believe is compromised.
exception.compensatingControl: An operator can rotate a credential out of band by re-running the seed with a new password; docs/runbook.md is the place that would document it.

requirements.statement: No account with a publicly known password exists in a deployed instance
requirements.source: OWASP ASVS 5.0.0 L1 V6.3.2 via docs/evidence/security-baseline.json

exception.reason: Accounts with passwords published in this repository are created by backend/app/db.py so the end-to-end suites have something to sign in as. Anyone who runs the seed against a reachable instance has handed out an admin account. The seed is what makes the E2E evidence reproducible, so removing it would remove the proof that the app works.
exception.compensatingControl: Seeding is a separate explicit command and is not part of the container start path; docs/runbook.md treats seeded data as development data.

requirements.statement: How fast a vulnerable third-party component must be replaced is written down
requirements.source: OWASP ASVS 5.0.0 L1 V15.1.1 via docs/evidence/security-baseline.json

exception.reason: Dependencies are audited on every CI run and re-audited weekly, but no document states the risk-based time frame within which a finding must be remediated, so "audited" has no deadline attached to it and a known finding could sit indefinitely without breaking a rule.
exception.compensatingControl: The dependency-scan control is required at R3 and fails the build on unaddressed findings, and EP-010 re-runs the audit weekly, so a new advisory turns CI red without anyone deciding to look.

requirements.statement: A request path cannot be turned into a filesystem path outside the directory the application intends to serve
requirements.source: OWASP ASVS 5.0.0 L1 V5.3.2 via docs/evidence/security-baseline.json

exception.reason: The single-page-app fallback joins the request path onto the static directory to decide whether a real file exists. The web framework is expected to normalise traversal sequences before the handler runs, and no test in this repository proves that it does. Recorded as unverified rather than claimed as safe, because an assumption about someone else's framework is not evidence.
exception.compensatingControl: The static directory contains build output only, the container runs the application as a non-root user, and nothing writes to that directory at runtime.

requirements.statement: Every component shipped in the dependency tree carries a licence that grants the right to use and redistribute it

exception.reason: The SBOM resolves no licence at all for 30 components in the Python tree, where the SBOM generator resolves no licence metadata for distributions that declare it only in free-text classifiers. A component with no resolvable licence is not permissively licensed, it is a component with no grant, so the obligation is unanswered rather than merely undocumented. Surfaced by the first licence review on 2026-09-23; resolving it means reading each publisher metadata by hand or improving the generator, neither of which is a reference app's job to prove.
exception.compensatingControl: The SBOM is shipped and pinned by digest, so which components are unresolved is visible rather than hidden, and the count is re-derived on every run of npm run check.
